title: Think Big Build Small
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This entry addresses the paralysis leaders often feel when facing an intimidating, large-scale vision, where overplanning becomes a socially acceptable form of procrastination. The recommended motto, 'Think Big, Build Small,' separates articulating an ambitious, unconstrained vision from immediately translating it into small, concrete first steps that can be started without heavy resources. The piece warns that big thinking without small building leads to overwhelm and perfectionism, while small building without big thinking produces busywork and misalignment. It closes by framing the motto as a way to know where you're going while still actually getting there.
points: Facing an intimidating big vision often causes leaders to overplan as a form of avoidance.
The 'Think Big, Build Small' motto separates articulating an ambitious vision from taking small, immediate first steps.
Small steps should prioritize simplicity and require no external resources to get started.
Big thinking alone produces overwhelm; small building alone produces busywork — the motto embraces both.
quotes: Acting on a big, audacious goal or vision can be intimidating.
Sometimes leaders overthink and plan excessively just to avoid taking the first uncomfortable step.
When approaching a massive project, long-range vision, or game-changing initiative, the best leaders Think Big, Build Small.
This approach helps leaders to separate direction and execution, allowing the brain to gain a foothold from which to take the first step.
Big thinking without building small leads to being overwhelmed, indecision, and perfectionism.
Good leaders think big so they know where they’re going. They build small so they actually get there.
